title: Content-standards violation scanner and classifier
description:
Scans every project issue and in-scope document against the canonical content-standards rules and classifies each violation found as mechanically fixable or judgment-requiring.

## Background

The canonical rules live in `docs/reference/jit-content-standards.md`: required issue-description structure (summary, `## Background`, `## Success Criteria`, optional `## Notes`), `[hard]`/`[aspirational]` `REQ-NN` markers on every criterion, clean titles free of embedded ids or ordinals, and standalone-readability (no undefined context, no reliance on a sibling issue). Some violations follow one fixed, unambiguous correction — an unmarked criterion, an embedded id in a title, a missing `## Success Criteria` heading — and are mechanical. Others need a reader's judgment, such as whether a description is actually understandable without outside context, and cannot be corrected by rule.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A scan pass evaluates the title and description of every issue in the project's issue store, every markdown document under `docs/`, and every live document under `dev/active/` (per the documentation lifecycle in `.jit/config.toml`'s `[documentation]` section), against every rule in `docs/reference/jit-content-standards.md`.
- [hard] REQ-02: Each finding records the offending issue or document, the specific rule violated, and a classification of `mechanical` or `judgment`.
- [hard] REQ-03: The classification covers, at minimum, these mechanical cases: an unmarked or malformed `[hard]`/`[aspirational]` `REQ-NN` criterion, an embedded id or ordinal in a title, and a missing `## Success Criteria` heading; and this judgment case: whether a description reads as standalone without outside context.
- [hard] REQ-04: Running the scan twice against an unchanged project produces identical findings.

## Notes

Archived documents (`dev/archive/`, `dev/sessions/`, `dev/studies/`, and `dev/active/` documents whose owning issue is Done) are historical record and out of scope for this scan.
